scams.name: Puerto Escondido Airport (PXM) & Oaxaca-Transfer Taxi Overcharge
scams.description: Puerto Escondido is reached via small Puerto Escondido Airport (PXM) or 7-hour drive/bus from Oaxaca City. Community reports from 2025 cover car-hire questions, one-way rentals from Oaxaca Airport, public-transport options between Puerto Escondido town and Mazunte, and last-minute accommodation. Legitimate fares: PXM airport to Zicatela (7 km, 15 min) via official Transporte Terrestre prepaid MX$250-350; Uber has limited availability in Puerto Escondido but does work — MX$150-250 when available. Oaxaca-Puerto Escondido via ADO bus MX$380-480 (7-hour night bus, safer than driving); via flight MX$1,800-2,500 (45 min). The 2025 scam patterns: (a) PXM arrivals-kerb kiosks quoting MX$600-1,000 for Zicatela transfer (2-3x real); (b) 'VIP private driver' at MX$1,500 for standard sedan; (c) 'combined PXM + Mazunte tour US$80' bundled; (d) Oaxaca rental-car agencies offering 'one-way to Puerto Escondido' with MX$3,000-5,000 'one-way drop fee' (real fair rate MX$1,200-2,000); (e) hotel concierge 'recommended transfer' at 2x Uber rate; (f) colectivos at ADO terminal overcharging foreigners ('foreign fare MX$150 per person' vs real MX$40); (g) 'surf camp transfer' bundle at 3x independent cost; (h) Mazunte day-trip 'private driver' at US$80 one-way (real public transport MX$40-60). For older travelers: (1) at PXM airport, use official Transporte Terrestre prepaid booth inside arrivals at MX$250-350 to Zicatela; Uber works but supply is thin — try first with 5-10 min wait patience; (2) from Oaxaca City, take ADO primera-clase night bus at MX$380-480 (7-hour comfortable) vs 7-hour drive via winding mountain road (NOT recommended at night or for older travelers); (3) IGNORE every 'VIP driver' upsell above MX$500; (4) for Mazunte day-trip (70 km east), take public colectivo MX$40-60 OR Uber MX$350-500 one-way; (5) for long-term accommodation, book via Booking.com or Hotels.com; AVOID WhatsApp/Instagram private sellers; (6) community reports list 2025 transit specifics for Puerto Escondido to Mazunte; (7) save Puerto Escondido Tourist Police +52 954 582 0175.
scams.avoidance: Transporte Terrestre prepaid booth PXM-Zicatela: MX$250-350 Oaxaca-PE via ADO primera-clase night bus MX$380-480 (7-hour safe) Mazunte day-trip: colectivo MX$40-60 or Uber MX$350-500 Book accommodation via Booking.com/Hotels.com (not WhatsApp) Tourist Police +52 954 582 0175
scams.location: Puerto Escondido Airport (PXM) arrivals, Oaxaca Airport (OAX) transfer pickup, Zicatela Beach drop-offs, La Punta taxi queue, hotel-lobby transfer desks

scams.name: Puerto Escondido Surf-School & Board-Rental Overcharge & Damage Scam
scams.description: Puerto Escondido's 'Mexican Pipeline' at Zicatela Beach is a world-class surf destination and hosts a 2025 surf-school and board-rental overcharge ecosystem. Community reports from 2025 cover surf-spot recommendations for intermediate surfers and beach-destination comparisons from Mexico City. Legitimate costs: Board rental at reputable shops: shortboard MX$250-400 per 4 hours; longboard MX$350-500. Surf lesson MX$500-800 per 2 hours (one-on-one) or MX$350-500 (group). Zicatela Beach is for EXPERIENCED surfers only (8-25 ft waves); La Punta (Puerto Escondido's west end) and Playa Carrizalillo are beginner/intermediate friendly. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) Zicatela beach-approach 'instructor' offering 'private lesson US$80' for non-qualified individuals (real school instructors have SERF or SERM certification); (b) board-rental 'pre-damage' fraud — unphotographed dings claimed as 'tourist damage' at return with US$80-200 demands; (c) 'surf camp all-inclusive US$600/week' with bait-and-switch accommodations and instruction quality; (d) 'Zicatela beginner lesson US$120' (Zicatela is too dangerous for beginners — this IS a scam by definition); (e) 'broken fin repair fee MX$800' for minor surface dings; (f) 'premium longboard US$60/day' for same board rentable at US$25 elsewhere; (g) hotel-concierge kickback where 'recommended surf school' is 1.5-2x Google-verified shop; (h) 'wetsuit rental MX$200/day' where wetsuits are often included in package. For older travelers — and especially non-strong swimmers: (1) DO NOT attempt surf at Zicatela 'Mexican Pipeline' — waves are 8-25 ft and have caused documented drownings; (2) for beginner/intermediate surf, choose La Punta or Playa Carrizalillo (gentler waves, beginner-friendly); (3) book surf lessons ONLY at Google 4.7+ schools: Puerto Surf School, Oasis Surf, Mexpipe Surf Academy — MX$500-800 per 2-hour one-on-one; (4) verify instructor has SERF/SERM certification; (5) photograph board condition BEFORE leaving rental shop; document every scratch/ding with timestamp; (6) REFUSE beach-approach 'instructor' offers without verifiable certification; (7) for surf camps, book established operators via Booking.com (Selina Hostels has surf-lesson add-ons); (8) community reports list 2025 surf-spot recommendations for intermediates; (9) remember Zicatela water-safety: never surf alone, always wear leash, respect lifeguard warnings.
scams.avoidance: Book Google 4.7+ schools: Puerto Surf School, Oasis Surf, Mexpipe Beginners: La Punta or Playa Carrizalillo (not Zicatela) Verify instructor SERF/SERM certification PHOTOGRAPH board condition BEFORE leaving rental shop Wetsuit typically included in package; refuse MX$200/day add-on
scams.location: Zicatela Beach surf rental shops, La Punta surf schools, Playa Carrizalillo board-rental kiosks, hotel-adjacent surf operators, 'instructor' beach approaches

scams.name: Puerto Escondido Beach-Tour Unlicensed Boat & Turtle/Dolphin Operator
scams.description: Puerto Escondido's iconic boat experiences — morning dolphin + turtle sighting, Manialtepec Lagoon bioluminescence (Aug-Dec), turtle-release at Playa Bacocho (year-round) — host a 2025 unlicensed-operator ecosystem. Community reports from 2025 cover trip planning and beach-destination comparisons. Legitimate costs: Dolphin + sea-turtle morning boat tour MX$400-700 per person (2-3 hours from Playa Principal). Manialtepec Lagoon bioluminescence + bird tour MX$500-800 per person (3-4 hour evening, Aug-Dec only). Turtle release at Playa Bacocho / Playa Escobilla: MX$100-200 entry fee (legitimate conservation program). The 2025 scam patterns: (a) Playa Principal touts selling 'private dolphin boat MX$2,500' when group tour is MX$500; (b) 'VIP bioluminescence MX$1,800 per person' when group tour is MX$700; (c) 'guaranteed dolphin/turtle sighting MX$300 extra' (wildlife can't be guaranteed; this is fraud); (d) unlicensed boats without life jackets, VHF radio, or insurance; (e) 'mandatory marine-park fee MX$200' at the boat launch (no such mandatory fee exists for Puerto Escondido tours); (f) off-season (Jan-July) bioluminescence offers — plankton is minimal; (g) 'private turtle-release ceremony US$80 per person' when conservation programs accept donations of MX$100-200; (h) 'swim with dolphins US$120 per person' — dolphins in wild are not to be swum with (ethical concern + illegal); tourists who 'swim' get charged extra for cordoned-off setup. For older travelers: (1) book boat tours ONLY via Google 4.7+ operators: Lalo Ecotours (Manialtepec specialist), Playa Principal Tours, Hidden Voyages — MX$400-800 per person group tour; (2) VERIFY life jackets, VHF radio, and captain license BEFORE boarding; (3) REFUSE 'private' upsells — group tours are same experience at 1/5th cost; (4) for Manialtepec bioluminescence, only book Aug-Dec on dark-moon nights; (5) REFUSE 'guaranteed sighting' upcharges — wildlife unpredictable; (6) for turtle release, go to Playa Bacocho at 5-6 PM, pay conservation fee MX$100-200, observe ethical release; AVOID 'private ceremony' upsells; (7) do NOT participate in 'swim with wild dolphins' — unethical and illegal; (8) motion-sickness meds helpful — open Pacific can be rough; (9) for older travelers with mobility concerns, boat-dock boarding can be slippery — request help or pass on tour; (10) bring biodegradable sunscreen for marine-safety.
scams.avoidance: Book Google 4.7+ operators: Lalo Ecotours, Playa Principal Tours Verify life jackets, VHF radio, captain license BEFORE boarding Manialtepec bioluminescence ONLY Aug-Dec dark-moon nights Turtle release at Playa Bacocho 5-6 PM with MX$100-200 conservation fee Refuse 'swim with wild dolphins' (illegal + unethical)
scams.location: Playa Principal boat launches, Manialtepec Lagoon (bioluminescence + birds), Playa Bacocho turtle-release center, La Punta tour-booking booths

scams.name: Puerto Escondido Zicatela & La Punta Restaurant Tourist-Menu Padding
scams.description: Puerto Escondido's Zicatela beachfront and La Punta surf-strip host a 2025 tourist-menu bill-padding ecosystem common to Mexican beach destinations. Community reports from 2025 cover accommodation and the broader trip-planning landscape. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) Zicatela beachfront restaurants with English-only menus at 2-3x local prices (fish taco MX$120 tourist vs MX$40 at Mercado Benito Juárez); (b) 'gratuity 18%' pre-added + tip line (double-tipping); (c) 'credit-card processing 10-15%' announced at bill; (d) 'seafood market price' at MX$1,500 lobster without weight disclosed; (e) 'complimentary guacamole' arriving as MX$180 line item; (f) USD-priced menus padding 10-15% exchange; (g) 'live music service MX$100/person' added unannounced; (h) La Punta surf-bar 'tequila shots buy 3 get 1 free' where 'free' is the overpriced one; (i) 'premium mezcal flight US$45' at standard mezcal. For older travelers: (1) eat at AUTHENTIC Puerto Escondido spots 2-3 blocks off Zicatela: Mi Pequeño Mundo (Mercado Benito Juárez), La Hosteria (authentic Oaxacan, Google 4.7+), Espadín Mezcal Bar (transparent mezcal pricing), Restaurante Los Tios (seafood); (2) Zicatela beachfront reputable: Almoraduz (Google 4.7+ with printed menu), Espresso Bar — budget MX$250-400 per meal; (3) La Punta has shifted to more 'digital nomad' prices — expect US$15-25 per meal at reputable Nautilo, Lychee; (4) INSPECT bill — refuse 'gratuity + tip' double; confirm card surcharge 0-3%; (5) request MX$ bill (not USD); (6) seafood: agree weight × price/kg IN WRITING; (7) refuse uninvited 'complimentary' appetizers; (8) for budget eats, Mercado Benito Juárez (Rinconada) has authentic Oaxacan at MX$60-120 per meal; (9) tequila/mezcal buy at Chedraui (Rinconada) not bars — bottle MX$400-1,000 vs bar MX$200 per shot; (10) community reports list 2025 restaurant picks for couples.
scams.avoidance: Eat off Zicatela: Mi Pequeño Mundo, La Hosteria, Los Tios at MX$250-400 Zicatela reputable: Almoraduz, Espresso Bar with printed menu Budget: Mercado Benito Juárez authentic MX$60-120 per meal Inspect bill; refuse double-tipping; card 0-3% Seafood: weight × price/kg IN WRITING; request MX$ bill
scams.location: Zicatela main beachfront restaurants, La Punta surf-bar strip, Rinconada tourist dining, Centro Mercado Zicatela tourist-menu venues

scams.name: Puerto Escondido Airbnb Surf-House Fake-Listing & Long-Term Rental Fraud
scams.description: Puerto Escondido's 2020-2025 digital-nomad + surf-tourism boom has outpaced legitimate accommodation supply, creating a 2025 fake-listing ecosystem. Community reports from 2025 cover last-minute accommodation, couple-travel planning, and surf-spot recommendations. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) Instagram DM/Facebook 'exclusive surf house' listings using stolen photos — properties don't exist or are 200-500m from surf; (b) WhatsApp-only 'digital-nomad monthly rental' demanding full-month payment upfront via bank transfer; (c) confirmed-booking cancellations during peak season (Dec-Feb, Jun-Aug Mexican Pipeline) with re-listing at 3-5x rate; (d) fake 'beachfront surf camp' where the 'beachfront' is actually 300m+ inland; (e) 'all-inclusive surf + accommodation + lessons US$1,200/week' bait-and-switch quality; (f) 'deposit US$500 to secure' non-refundable bank transfer; (g) on-arrival bait-and-switch to inferior property; (h) 'cleaning deposit US$200 cash' that never returns; (i) 'mandatory weekly cleaning fee US$80' added unexpectedly mid-stay. For older travelers: (1) book ONLY via Booking.com, Hotels.com, Airbnb (platform-protected); or direct from verified hotel websites (Selina Hostels, Hotel Santa Fe, Bungalows Pacífico) — all with Booking.com 4.6+ ratings; (2) NEVER bank-transfer to Instagram DM or WhatsApp private sellers; platform secure payment only; (3) cross-reference property name + photos on Google Maps + Tripadvisor BEFORE booking — fake if zero independent results; (4) for peak season (Dec-Feb, Jun-Aug), book 3-6 months ahead on Booking.com with free cancellation; (5) AVOID Airbnb for peak season on Puerto Escondido — Mexican Airbnb cancellation pattern is documented; (6) for monthly digital-nomad stays, prefer Selina Hostels or verified co-living spaces (Casa Wabi Surf, Boulder Guesthouse); (7) photograph property condition on arrival; (8) confirm 'beachfront' vs 'beach access' in writing — 200m 'walk to beach' is common misleading claim; (9) community reports list 2025 specific housing warnings.
scams.avoidance: Book ONLY via Booking.com, Hotels.com, Airbnb (platform-protected) Reputable: Selina Hostels, Hotel Santa Fe, Bungalows Pacífico (4.6+) NEVER bank-transfer to Instagram/WhatsApp private sellers Cross-reference name + photos on Google Maps + Tripadvisor Peak season (Dec-Feb, Jun-Aug): book 3-6 months ahead
scams.location: Airbnb/Booking.com Puerto Escondido listings, Instagram 'PE Surf House' DMs, Facebook 'Puerto Escondido Rentals' groups, WhatsApp-only digital-nomad housing offers

scams.name: Puerto Escondido Beach Vendor & 'Massage on the Beach' Pressure Scam
scams.description: Puerto Escondido's beaches host an active 2025 vendor-culture similar to Puerto Vallarta's Playa Los Muertos. Community reports from 2025 cover trip planning and beach-destination comparisons. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) beach vendors walking up with sarongs, jewelry, henna, coconuts — 'whatever you want to pay' pitch that becomes MX$500-1,200 demand; (b) 'free henna tattoo' that becomes MX$400 when trying to leave; (c) 'massage on the beach MX$400 for 60 min' that ends with MX$1,200 'extended service' bill; (d) 'fruit vendor buy 2 get 1 free' where 'free' is the overpriced one; (e) 'friendly local photographer' offering to take family photo with YOUR phone, demanding MX$200-500 'tip'; (f) 'beach-chair rental US$25' at free public sand; (g) 'surfboard leash rental MX$100' at beach shop with included leash in board rental; (h) 'snorkel mask rental MX$200' at Playa Carrizalillo (included in beach-club access MX$50). For older travelers: (1) firm 'no gracias' and keep walking — don't stop or engage vendors; (2) all Puerto Escondido beaches are PUBLIC federal property — no entrance fee or chair 'rental' on sand is mandatory; legitimate beach clubs offer chair + umbrella MX$100-200 with drink/food minimum; (3) REFUSE every 'free' offer — henna, photos, fruit — if accepted, negotiate and agree price BEFORE service; (4) for beach massage, book at inland spa (Spa Ecológico Pochote, Temazcal Zicatela) at MX$800-1,500 for 60-90 min authentic; (5) take photos yourself with phone timer OR ask a restaurant server; (6) refuse 'beach-chair rental US$25' — walk to sand and sit on towel; (7) for snorkel at Playa Carrizalillo, buy own mask/snorkel at OXXO MX$150 (total purchase) vs MX$200/day rental; (8) for coconut vendor, ask price BEFORE and have small bills ready; fair MX$50-80 per opened coconut; (9) Playa Carrizalillo is the most vendor-dense beach; Playa Principal is calmer; La Punta at sunset is party-dense (louder vendor culture).
scams.avoidance: Firm 'no gracias' and keep walking; no engagement Beaches are PUBLIC — no mandatory chair rental on sand REFUSE 'free' offers; negotiate price BEFORE any service Beach massage: book inland at Pochote or Temazcal Zicatela Buy own snorkel mask at OXXO MX$150 total (not MX$200/day rent)
scams.location: Zicatela beachfront, Playa Carrizalillo, Playa Principal, La Punta sunset zone, beach-vendor commercial stretches
